newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux says Europe behind profit fall.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux says Europe behind profit fall.

text.p: Swedish appliance maker Electrolux AB Friday posted a 19 percent fall in profits for 1996 and, echoing rival Whirlpool Corp., blamed a weaker European market.
Improved markets in North America and other parts of the world counter-balanced the fall, the company said, forecasting a strong U.S. market in the coming quarters.
"The markets are still sluggish in Germany, France and Italy, but you can expect an upturn," Chief Executive Leif Johansson told a news conference.
"Our opinion is that (the U.S. market) feels strong in the coming quarters," he added.

Electrolux posted a profit of 3.25 billion crowns ($450.6 million) compared with 4.02 billion crowns ($557.4 million) for 1995. Sales fell 5 percent to 110 billion crowns ($15.2 billion) compared with a year earlier.

Competitor Whirlpool Corp., the biggest maker of home appliances in the United States, Tuesday reported a sharp rebound in earnings for the latest quarter, thanks to outstanding gains in North American and Latin American markets.
